method.primary: Visible scene-graph inventory after real material batching and instancing. Triangles include instance counts; bytes count unique geometry attributes and indices, excluding textures/driver storage. This is deterministic submitted-geometry potential, not frustum-culling-aware renderer timings or GPU-memory telemetry.
method.sourceIsolation: Fresh git archive of features, lib, scripts, package.json and package-lock.json at baselineRevision; only installed node_modules shared by symlink. No environment files, stores, uploads or secrets copied. Baseline source checkout removed after successful comparison.
method.versions: Baseline archive versus current source, every one of 44 transitive source hashes checked against the frozen visual source manifest before emitting this report.
method.modelState: Production createSpacecraft(THREE); setLayout(wide/compact), update(0, home, true, {activeRoom: home, layout, delta: 0, immediateDoors: true}); updateMatrixWorld(true). Real production material batches and static instances.
method.meshCount: Visible mesh nodes below the traversed root, after batching; draw-call candidates, not observed renderer draw calls. Instanced meshes count as one node.
method.triangleCount: Index count or position count / 3, multiplied by each InstancedMesh count. Does not account for frustum culling or additional rendering passes.
method.geometryArrayBytes: Sum of indices and geometry attributes once per unique geometry within each inventory. Excludes instanceMatrix/instanceColor arrays, texture allocations, transient arrays, driver resources and actual process/GPU memory.
method.namedGroupVisibility: Named subgroup inventories traverseVisible from that subgroup; hidden ancestors are not included in Three.js traversal checks. groupEffectiveVisibility records full ancestor visibility. Both exterior variants are deliberately inventoried as authored subgroups; whole-scene inventory includes only the currently visible variant.
method.retainedSceneGraph: Separate traverse (not traverseVisible) of the full production scene graph includes hidden layout variants. It excludes detached source solids, geometry caches and objects no longer retained by this graph; it is not a complete application-memory measurement.
method.supplemental: Same inventory method for named shared, ladder, service, exterior and cabin groups. JSON deep-copy each full layout snapshot immediately before switching layouts; compare exact serialized fields, inventories and fingerprints.
method.fingerprint: SHA-256 in visible subtree traversal order over mesh world matrix, semantic parts, instance count, material color/emissive/emissiveIntensity/roughness/metalness/opacity/transparency/side; sorted geometry attribute/index names, item sizes, normalization, typed array types and raw bytes; instanceMatrix bytes where present. Texture pixels, shader output and transient object IDs are excluded.
method.linerSelection: Visible production meshes whose name or userData.parts contains walkway-continuous-rear-liner. Result is the single walkway-plain-cabin-enamel mesh with only that source part; no proxy geometry.
method.ladderWithoutServiceSpine: Visible meshes under left-vertical-walkway excluding meshes whose name or semantic parts begins service-spine-. Uses actual production geometry/materials/transforms. The separate wall isolation cassette is outside this named ladder group and compared separately.

fixture.browser: No browser or WebGL used for this structural inventory; rendered verification is separately recorded in the evidence README.
fixture.canvasArtwork: Node fixture uses the production non-browser artwork fallback; no real texture rendering, display artwork or GPU allocation measured.

limitations: These are deterministic geometry inventories, not browser performance results, timing, temperature, power, battery-life or memory measurements.
Visible scene-graph mesh candidates are not frustum-culling-aware and do not include shadow, AO, postprocessing or other extra render-pass submissions. Do not equate them with observed draws.
Nested inventories overlap. Service-spine, whole-ladder and whole-scene deltas describe the same changed geometry and must not be added together. Bytes deduplicate only within each named inventory.
Retained scene-graph geometry is distinct from visible submitted-geometry potential and is still not the complete set of resources retained by the application or GPU.
Exact structural/framing/route snapshots at home and time zero do not replace live navigation, interaction, responsive rendered checks or aesthetic review.
interpretation: The open rail carriers and quieter rung hardware change the intended design. They yield 7,584 fewer triangles, one fewer mesh candidate and 202,464 fewer geometry-array bytes in each visible whole-model layout. This does not establish a speed, memory, heat or battery improvement.

The service spine has 69,208 triangles in 17 mesh candidates after the change. The whole ladder subgroup has 118,980 triangles in 36 mesh candidates. The separate isolation cassette remains 5,520 triangles in four mesh candidates.

All four approved cabins, paired stowed spanners, end grip equipment, continuous liner, docking, service assembly and exterior groups have identical measured geometry/material/transform fingerprints and inventories. Shared camera framing, aperture bounds, routes, iris poses and passage lining snapshots are exactly preserved.

The support metadata intentionally replaces the obsolete broad backing datum (-0.936) with the new carrier face datum (-0.943). Rail/rung arrangement, worklights, terminal light positions and rail ends are unchanged.
